key_insight: Nanosecond DBD plasma on a blunt body creates two separate hypersonic perturbations—a brief shock and a longer-lived thermal wake—whose strength and extent depend strongly on local pressure and temperature.
engineering_relevance: These findings matter for hypersonic transition control because the actuator can alter both shock structure and near-wall heating, potentially affecting boundary-layer stability independently.
method: Mach 6 Ludwieg-tube tests on a generic blunt body with a nanosecond-pulsed DBD actuator
Quiescent ambient-pressure experiments matched to predicted nose-region conditions
Pulse-energy measurement plus schlieren imaging to track shock and thermal disturbance evolution
evidence_signal: Schlieren and energy measurements showed that lower pressure reduced deposited energy, weakened the actuator shock, enlarged the heated region, and in Mach 6 flow temporarily increased bow-shock stand-off distance by about 11%.
watch_item: Because actuator behavior changes with local thermodynamic conditions, results from one pressure/flow regime may not transfer directly to another hypersonic configuration.
paper_title: Nanosecond DBD-Induced Shock and Thermal Perturbations on Blunt Bodies in Hypersonic Flow
